stories.title: Largest Electric Bus Fleet in New York to Serve Bronx Neighborhood Elevated Asthma Rates
stories.label: health
stories.summary: New York State's largest fleet of electric school buses is now on the road in the South Bronx, a neighborhood where kids have more than double the national rate of asthma. The family-owned bus company has been serving children with special needs there for over 30 years, and now those rides will be cleaner and quieter. Swapping diesel engines for electric ones means less exhaust pumped into a community that already struggles to breathe easy. It's a simple, real-world fix aimed straight at protecting children's lungs every single school day.
stories.why_good: A concrete, already-implemented change that directly reduces air pollution exposure for children in a neighborhood with documented health harm.

stories.title: Algeria Returns Kindness Shown by Kansans Who Welcomed its World Cup Team with the Trip of a Lifetime
stories.label: people
stories.summary: Earlier this year, families in Kansas welcomed Algeria's World Cup team with open arms during their stay in the state. Algeria didn't forget that warmth, and this month flew a group of those same Kansas families to Algeria as a thank-you. When the exhausted travelers landed at 4:30 a.m., they were greeted by flowers, hugs, and dozens of government and hospitality officials who wanted to return the favor. It's a lovely reminder that kindness between strangers can turn into lasting friendship between whole communities.
stories.why_good: A real act of international goodwill that actually happened, showing ordinary generosity being repaid across borders with no political angle.
